1.mascotDialogue: All the splitting is just bookkeeping — the actual sorting happens entirely in the merge step, comparing two already-sorted halves and interleaving them correctly.

2.mascotDialogue: Lines 9 and 10 are the merge's heart: compare the fronts of both halves, take the smaller, advance only that side. Lines 12 and 13 mop up whichever half still has leftovers once the other runs out.

3.mascotDialogue: This view doesn't show swaps at all — merge sort doesn't swap elements in place, it writes the smaller of two fronts into a fresh position, every comparison.

4.mascotDialogue: It's easy to think the merge is finished the moment the main comparison loop ends — but one side almost always finishes before the other, and forgetting to drain the leftovers loses data, silently.
